items.title: 5 checks before you pick a vector database
points: Vector databases store AI-searchable data by meaning rather than keywords (matching intent/context instead of exact words), making them critical infrastructure for chatbots, agents, and search systems.
Most disappointing AI results stem from poor data retrieval upstream, not the underlying model itself.
AWS Marketplace released an evaluation guide covering 5 key checks: architecture patterns, hybrid search capabilities, scaling, hosting trade-offs, embedding pipeline fit, and metadata filtering.

Vector databases underpin three AI patterns: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG, where systems pull relevant context from your own data instead of relying solely on model training), agentic memory (semantic recall across sessions without replaying full histories), and semantic search (matching by intent).

Evaluation should include hybrid search support (dense vector search plus keyword-based retrieval), scaling/hosting options, embedding pipeline compatibility with data workflows, and metadata filtering alongside semantic similarity.
The guide includes architecture diagrams for RAG and agentic workflows using Amazon Bedrock, with free trials available on AWS Marketplace to test before committing.

sections.title: Why Vector Databases Matter for AI Projects
points: Most AI disappointing results stem from poor data retrieval upstream, not the model itself.
Vector databases enable meaning-based search—matching user intent and context—rather than simple keyword matching.

They power three critical AI patterns: retrieving relevant context for responses (RAG), maintaining agent memory across sessions without replaying full histories, and finding semantically similar content.

sections.title: What to Evaluate When Choosing a Vector Database
points: Hybrid search capabilities: assess whether the database handles both dense vector search and keyword-based retrieval.
Scaling and hosting options: determine if the solution meets your performance requirements and deployment preferences.
Embedding pipeline fit: evaluate compatibility with your data ingestion and transformation workflows.
Metadata filtering: confirm the system can efficiently filter results based on structured attributes alongside semantic similarity.
